anchor.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must recognize, and not report, a #[cfg(unix)] transport or adapter function or match arm that sits beside a loopback TCP enum variant or function with no #[cfg] guard, which Windows uses instead.
anchor.scope: The item changes when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] item in crates/sc-lint-portability.

item.title: fixture
item.text: PORT-010 still reports the #[cfg(unix)] Unix-socket match arm even though the TcpLoopback enum variant beside it has no #[cfg] guard and serves Windows.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` describe work that changes when sc-lint's PORT-010 rule reports or stops reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` item in crates/sc-lint-portability, as described in `anchor.scope`? Work on PORT-010 counts whichever `#[cfg(unix)]` shape or sibling it handles, and an item that decides to leave PORT-010's reporting of such items unchanged also counts. Work on another rule (for example another PORT-0xx rule), on another feature such as dependency ownership or boundaries, or on another crate does not count, even when it is in the same crate. Judge subject overlap only; do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.yes: The item changes, keeps, or directly depends on when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` item.
criteria.no: The item is about another rule, another feature, or another crate, and does not touch when PORT-010 reports `#[cfg(unix)]` items.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions portability linting but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010's reporting of `#[cfg(unix)]` items is affected.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` names one shape that PORT-010 must recognize and not report: a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm that sits beside a loopback TCP sibling (an enum variant or a function) that has no `#[cfg]` guard and is what Windows uses. Does `item.text` plan or report that PORT-010 stops reporting this shape? The loopback TCP sibling is the defining feature; other siblings (a same-name `#[cfg(windows)]` function, a `#[cfg(windows)]` named-pipe variant) are different shapes. A general promise to review or fix PORT-010 false positives does not name this shape. Judge presence only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.yes: The item says PORT-010 stops reporting, skips, or treats as covered a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm because a loopback TCP enum variant or function without a `#[cfg]` guard beside it serves Windows. Words such as TCP loopback, localhost TCP, TcpLoopback, un-gated or unguarded count. Extra conditions that keep reporting other cases are allowed.
criteria.no: The item does not plan this shape: it is silent about an unguarded loopback TCP sibling, handles only a different sibling shape, speaks only of false positives in general, or says PORT-010 keeps reporting the shape.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions an unguarded loopback TCP sibling and PORT-010 but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 is to stop reporting the `#[cfg(unix)]` item.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that PORT-010 not report a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm when a loopback TCP sibling (enum variant or function) with no `#[cfg]` guard beside it serves Windows. Does `item.text` state a plan or outcome that cannot be reconciled with this, such as PORT-010 still reporting that shape, leaving PORT-010 unchanged for it, or relying on a consumer exclusion instead of the rule change? The requirement covers only unguarded siblings: still reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` item whose loopback TCP sibling is itself `#[cfg]`-guarded is not a conflict. Silence about the shape, or work on a different shape, is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item says PORT-010 still reports, keeps reporting, or is left unchanged for a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item beside an unguarded loopback TCP sibling that serves Windows, or says that shape is handled only by an exclusion.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item conflicts: it plans to stop reporting the shape, is silent about it, handles a different shape, or keeps reporting only when the loopback TCP sibling is itself `#[cfg]`-guarded.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions the shape and PORT-010 but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 will still report it.
